text:
You need a script editor who can catch grammar, syntax, and factual issues while keeping true crime content clear, consistent, and ready for tight deadlines.

Hi, I’m Noor Halden. I’m interested in your Script Editor role because the core of the job is the kind of detail-focused work I value: careful reading, clean structure, accurate wording, and consistent presentation across every script. I understand how important it is in true crime content to maintain clarity and credibility while also keeping the pacing engaging for the audience.

While my background is in machine learning and NLP, I bring a strong editing mindset to text-heavy work. My experience with Python, pandas, scikit-learn, PyTorch, LangChain, OpenAI API, Hugging Face Transformers, XGBoost, and machine learning has trained me to work with language systematically, notice inconsistencies, and review content with precision. I’m comfortable analyzing text for errors, checking for logic gaps, and making sure details stay aligned throughout a document.

For this role, I would approach each script by reviewing grammar, punctuation, spelling, and syntax first, then moving into fact-checking and consistency checks for names, dates, and references. I also understand the importance of readability and tone, especially when a script needs to sound polished and coherent across multiple sections. If something reads awkwardly or seems unclear, I would flag it and suggest a cleaner revision.

I’m also accustomed to working in environments where accuracy and deadlines both matter, and I would bring that same discipline to your production workflow. My goal would be to help your writers and producers deliver scripts that are polished, reliable, and easy to follow without losing their intended voice.

If selected, I would focus on being thorough, responsive, and collaborative so your team can move quickly without sacrificing quality. What does your current script review process look like, and would you like the editor to focus more on line-by-line corrections or broader content and fact-checking feedback?
